number.why: The published abstract explicitly reports the served HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90) for first-event 3-point MACE with semaglutide versus placebo. Follow-up and the registry's analysis population support the served labels. The registry reports a different upper confidence limit, which requires acknowledging but does not invalidate the abstract-derived number.

quotes.span: A primary cardiovascular end-point event occurred in 569 of the 8803 patients (6.5%) in the semaglutide group and in 701 of the 8801 patients (8.0%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90; P<0.001).
The primary cardiovascular end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke in a time-to-first-event analysis.
Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide at a dose of 2.4 mg or placebo.
the mean duration of follow-up was 39.8±9.4 months.
FAS included all randomised participants. All participants were analyzed according to the treatment to which they were assigned at randomisation.

entry.why: The enrolled population and randomized double-blind placebo-controlled design satisfy the question. Eligibility is narrower than all adults, restricting enrollment to age 45 or older and BMI at least 27, but remains within the requested population.

quotes.span: In a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, event-driven superiority trial, we enrolled patients 45 years of age or older who had preexisting cardiovascular disease and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of 27 or greater but no history of diabetes.

missed: The registry contains a directly reported HR, not merely counts for reconstructing a risk ratio: evidence/held/registry/NCT03574597.json states "RESULT OUTCOME 0 ANALYSIS 0: groups Semaglutide, Placebo | Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.80 (95% CI 0.72 to 0.89) | p < 0.0001 | METHOD Regression, Cox". Its upper confidence limit differs from the abstract's 0.90. The packet does not explain this discrepancy; retain the served abstract estimate while recording the source disagreement. Neither verdict changes.
